errata.disposition: restatement of a risk-register mitigation so it matches the shipped artifact - no formal spec amendment, no re-plan, no criteria change, no re-scoring
errata.trigger: An executed adversarial security review (M3) drove 253 Tier-1 tags / 200 captures for a SINGLE skill against R1's documented cap of 3 dw/skill/session, and reproduced it verbatim after the M4 fixes landed. The cap is keyed on (session_id, engram_id); session_id is caller-supplied and unauthenticated, session.resolve_id upserts any string, and OMITTING session_id mints a fresh UUID per call - so the documented, honest calling convention defeats it with no malice. R1's mitigation string therefore described a control that does not exist.
errata.what_changed: risks[R1].mitigation: 'two-phase commit, Tier-0 barred from S, Tier-1 capped 3 dw/skill/session at weight 0.6, metaplastic saturation, Dream-only S writes' -> an object-keyed and temporal statement of what actually ships: two-phase commit; Tier-0 barred from S; Dream-only S writes (G3); eph_tag as the sole plasticity-S input (eph_event never, now held by test); a per-engram refractory window on the R bump (eta_r_refractory_s=30s) so R counts occasions not calls; decay applied at read (lambda_R 0.1/day, lambda_S 0.01/day) so influence self-reverses without Dream, sync() or a human; spacing-gated potentiation (tau_spacing_hours=6.0) so a burst sets anchors and commits nothing; bounded retroactive credit (retroactive_credit_max=10); metaplastic saturation (bounds the per-event step, not the event count); Tier-1 weight 0.6. per_skill_session_cap=3 is RETAINED but demoted to runaway protection, not counted as an anti-poisoning control. The 'adversarial-noise robustness test in the ablation suite' clause is struck: it never shipped (eval/ablations.py has three switches, none adversarial; no AC covers it) and is carried forward as CF-1. R1's risk statement, tag (P0), owner and milestone (M3,M4) are unchanged - 'bounded, not eliminated' was always correct.
errata.why: FORGE section 4.2, structural result: a quota binds only if you can name principals and prevent free creation of principals. Under stdio local-first there is exactly ONE OS principal (client and server are the same user), session creation is free by design (each turn, each reconnect, each server process), and even a server-signed token does not help because the server would issue one to whoever asks. So no per-subject quota can bind in v1 without changing the deployment posture, which docs/02 defers. The bound must therefore move from the SUBJECT to the OBJECT: per engram, per wall-clock window - keyed on what a caller cannot mint. FORGE section 4.3: 'Under local-first stdio, Magicite's achievable integrity guarantee is temporal, not authenticational.' These object-keyed bounds are not v1 stopgaps: they survive into the deferred served profile, composing with per-tenant authorization rather than being replaced by it. A security claim a reader relies on and that does not hold is worse than an absent one.

Section 5.2: 'This is a spec edit and is not mine to make ... There is precedent for the vehicle: the recorded A1-REVISED entry that touched risks[R6] under declared variance. -> SPECTRA/RAMZA.'
errata.evidence: m3-security-review.md F-1 (executed) and m4-security-retest.md (executed post-fix against pinned commit 3660c5d, 324-test baseline on the extraction). Key measurements: 253 tags / 200 captures reproduce exactly; 200 captured Tier-1 tags -> delta S = 0.000000000; conversion needs >= ~85 min elapsed then at most ONE commit per engram per Dream run, ceiling +0.048/occasion; 30 calls across 30 minted sessions -> exactly ONE R bump (0.15), rank 7->5 not 7->3; 50 calls omitting session_id -> R unchanged; R pinned 1.0 with a 30d-old anchor -> back to baseline rank 7; 4200 captured edge tags -> 0 committed edges (max edge S 3.6e-07); 100 planted Tier-2 valence=+1.0 eph_event rows -> max |delta S| = 0.0; mutation spot-check 8/8 guards detected.

RES-2 cross-session credit hijack: a high-salience valence=-1.0 signal_outcome naming another agent's session retroactively credits that agent's live tags (2 skills at -1.0, executed); breadth is bounded to 10 by retroactive_credit_max but the hijack needs a participation check, i.e. identity or a tool-surface change (re-test section 5 D)
RES-3 pre-capture session suppression survives; bounded at M6 by session_end_tag_grace_s=60s. FORGE's N-7 as specified (make session_end non-suppressive) did not land (re-test section 5 A)

RES-4 saturation is reachable by a patient caller: +0.15 R ceiling ~95% in ~9.5 min, rank-3 flip in 12 min / 48 calls; S >= 0.6 in ~18 daily occasions. Deliberate - a local-first server cannot distinguish 'used often' from 'reported as used often' (FORGE section 3.1 part 3)

RES-5 co-activation row fan-out uncapped per call (380 edges from one 20-id call); an edge at S=0.06 moves a candidate further than R saturated at 1.0. Potentiation is gated so committed edge weight is noise (3.6e-07), but 'R is the routing lever' is no longer the right mental model
